newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE JUDGE'S DECISION ENDS STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE JUDGE'S DECISION ENDS STRIKE.

text.p: The 15-day-old strike by Argentine professional soccer players ended on Wednesday after a judge allowed six players at troubled side Deportivo Espanol to move to other teams.

"There will be football," Juan Sune, an official representing the professional players union, told local radio after judge Juan Garibotto's decision to accept the guarantees for the six players offered by the Argentine Football Association (AFA).
League matches scheduled for Wednesday afternoon were set to go ahead.

Garibotto had previously ruled that the six Deportivo players counted as assets of the heavily indebted club, meaning they could not move until all creditors had been paid even though their contracts expired on June 30.
Players protested against the decision, and decided to strike until their colleagues were released. Soccer fans spent two weekends without matches.
Earlier this week the AFA presented a financial guarantee of $2 million for the six players which the judge accepted Wednesday.
